knIntro: Market-blind Round-of-32 predictions of the 90-minute result — win, draw or loss (a draw is then settled by extra time and penalties, which we do not forecast). Eight independent statistical and machine-learning models rate every tie; a multi-calibrated blend pools them into one published call. No betting line or market price is read at any point. The already-played Canada–South Africa tie is left out. As each match finishes we score these calls in the open.

peStep1Copy: Any match, group winner, or title odds. Just ask.
peStep2Copy: Public data gathered by priority: recent results, club form, injuries and lineups, venue and weather. Every fact dated and sourced; odds pages discarded.
peStep3Copy: Live Elo gives win / draw / loss per match; qualification and title questions run 100,000 Monte-Carlo simulations.
peStep4Copy: Key evidence becomes a bounded shift on the prior — at most ±8 points per match, nothing moves without evidence. Every output carries a confidence tier.
peStep5Copy: Multilingual reports with full sources; every question Brier-scored in public after settlement — wrong calls stay on record.

kgIntro: Nine forecasters rate every tie from group-stage play alone. Here is how each one predicts and which on-pitch data it leans on.
kgFooter: Every model is market-blind: it reads only group-stage FIFA stats and team strength, never a betting line or market price.
kgDixonColes: A classic football scoreline model. It turns each team's group-stage attack and defence — expected goals for and against — into a most-likely-scoreline grid, with a correction for low-scoring draws.
kgXgElo: A strength rating updated across the group stage by how a team's chance quality (expected goals from its shots) compared with its opponent's — so the quality of chances created moves the ladder, not just the final score.
kgProdegy: Keeps a separate attack rating and defence rating for each team, updating both from group-stage expected goals, then pits one side's attack against the other side's defence.
kgFatigueElo: A strength rating that also weighs physical load: teams that ran the most high-intensity distance in the group stage are docked a little for likely tiredness.
kgTacticalMelo: A style-clash model. Beyond raw strength it compares playing styles — possession, pressing and counter-attacking — so a matchup can favour the lower-rated side.
kgLinebreakGbm: A gradient-boosted machine-learning model trained on chance-creation and defence-penetration stats: shots, line-breaks and ball progressions.
kgPassnetRf: A random-forest machine-learning model trained on passing-structure and style stats: possession, pressing and build-up shape.
kgStackedEnsemble: A meta-model that learns how to weight and combine the seven base models' views into one read.
kgMulticalibrated: The published pick. It pools all eight models into one consensus, then applies a small bias correction learned on the group stage, bounded so it stays close to the consensus. Always market-blind.
